key_insight: Leading LLMs could generate varied colonoscopy-prep conversations, but correctness and safety varied enough that automated deferral safeguards were still needed.
clinical_relevance: For colonoscopy prep support, conversational AI may help answer patient questions, but outputs must be carefully checked to avoid unsafe or incorrect guidance.
method: Generated 250 synthetic patient-AI coach dialogues per model from five leading LLMs.
Used 3–7 question-answer pairs per dialogue on diet, medications, and prep topics.
Compared human and automatic ratings for correctness, harmfulness, difficulty, and diversity.
evidence_signal: The study used medical-expert review plus LLM-as-a-judge evaluation, and compared models with permutation tests and inter-rater agreement via Gwet’s AC1.
watch_item: Synthetic dialogue performance does not guarantee real-world patient safety, so deployment would require strong human oversight and reliable safety filtering.
paper_title: Evaluating Large Language Models for Colonoscopy Preparation Assistance: Correctness and Diversity in Synthetic Dialogues
